query: Should I commit our office to delivering the full coastal learning rollout?
target: Decline the full rollout commitment and offer the funded discovery phase.
calibrated: limit the commitment to evidence gathering
relation: The inland skills episode shows this user can withhold delivery volume until missing inputs are collected, while the literacy expansion shows the cost of promising full regional delivery before demand is verified; only both justify declining coastal rollout while offering funded discovery.
A: When an inland skills pilot arrived with only a concept sheet and no employer counts or delivery sites, I refused to put any delivery volume on the partner calendar and instead scheduled interviews to collect those missing inputs first.
B: On last year's literacy expansion, I told the partner forum we would deliver the full regional programme before usage figures arrived; when the reconciled data showed half the expected uptake, we had to revise the public commitment.
E1: The funding round closes in six weeks.
E2: The award form has a required ceiling field, and finance will not release funds until that field is filled.
B_prime: On last year's literacy expansion, I arranged a partner workshop and waited for attendance figures before naming a delivery scope; when the reconciled data arrived, the workshop confirmed interest but the counts still did not support a regional rollout.
lure: The programme director says an ambitious public announcement would strengthen the application.
